newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Malaysian deals dominate.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Malaysian deals dominate.

text.p: News of financings for Malaysian borrowers enlivened a slow Asian debt market on Monday.
Utility Tenaga Nasional plans to raise US$1 billion from local and foreign markets in the first quarter of this year, according to a report in a Malaysian newspaper.

Also from Malaysia, bankers said Sime International (L) Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Sime Bank, has mandated Fuji International Finance (HK), Development Bank of Singapore and LTCB Asia to arrange a US$100 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
The certificates will carry a maturity of three years and pay an all-in return of 26-28 basis ponts over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).

Malaysia's Shell Refining Co Bhd said it will sign a US$360 million loan facility agreement with a group of 12 offshore banks for the building of a Long Residue Catalytic Cracking complex on Wednesday.
The deal was arranged by Standard Chartered Bank Malaysia Bhd and Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank Bhd.
Elsewhere, more details were out on China Construction Holdings' US$30 million floating rate note issue.
The three-year notes will be priced at par to float at 200 basis points over LIBOR. With fees, the all-in return is 225 basis points to top tier managers.
BA Asia and KorAm Bank are arrangers.
The issuer is 43.4 percent owned by Gold Ram International, a wholly owned subsidiary of China's Ministry of Construction, which will issue a letter of undertaking to support the issue.

Hong Kong's Mass Transit Railway Corp signed a HK$5 billion revolving credit facility with 35 banks today. Finance director Clement Kwok said the Authority does not expect to engage in any new large-scale borrowings until the second half of 1997.
The MTRC estimates it will borrow about HK$10 billion this year.
